what_happened: The job "Open the job's PR early so CI runs during verification" (20261025-055626-er96) failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. The critic found the plan fit the request and the reading, and the code it names exists. The design was sound: write the marker right after the push, and send the lease-pinned replace through check_replace on both landing paths. It found one major problem. In production Athena::go switches to GhEarly, and the CLI integration tests call Athena::go directly. Those tests are not deliverables, so the producer cannot change them. At least two assert that no line contains "warning". Their fixtures have no GitHub origin, so GhEarly fails and the plan prints a warning: line. That breaks criterion 5 (cargo test fails). The plan left this to the producer to "check" and left it as open question 3. There were two minor findings. The plan does not say link.head must be updated to the landing commit after the replace and before the head check and merge guard. It also does not say where the gh Runner comes from, since Athena::go has none. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered.
cause: The planning stage is not required to find every existing caller and test that runs the code path it changes, or to settle each open question before it hands over the plan. The risk list and open questions can say "producer to check", and the template has no rule against that. Nothing ties the plan's new production behavior (a new Runner, a warning line) to the tests that assert on that output. The reading also drew the deliverable list narrowly, with the CLI tests left out, so the producer could not fix the conflict even if it found it. The critic finds this only by reading the tests, so it surfaces late. The three-round cap has no fallback: no partial plan is kept, the critic's findings are not carried into a retry, and the minor gaps (Runner source, link.head update) cost rounds too. The same late-critic pattern has failed other planning jobs on this branch.
prevention: Change the plan template and the planning checks. (1) For every production path the plan changes, the planner must list the existing callers and tests that run it (a search of the tests for the entry point and for output assertions) and say for each whether it still passes. Any test that would break must be added to the deliverables, or the design must change so it does not break. (2) Open questions and "producer to check" items that affect an acceptance criterion are not allowed in a plan sent to the critic; the planner must decide them. (3) The plan must name where each new dependency comes from at each entry point (such as the gh Runner in Athena::go) and which field is updated at which step. (4) Carry the critic's findings into the next round and into any retry.
proposed_request: Open the job's pull request early, right after the push, so CI runs during verification. Outcome: the PR exists before the verifier finishes, a marker is written right after the push, and the lease-pinned replace goes through check_replace on both landing paths. Planning requirements: before settling the design, search the CLI integration tests (crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs and others) for every test that calls Athena::go and for every assertion that no output line contains "warning". Decide in the plan how each stays green. Either the early-PR step is silent when the origin is not a GitHub remote, or the needed test files are listed as deliverables and changed. Do not leave this as an open question. State where the gh Runner for Athena::go comes from. State that link.head is set to the landing commit after the replace and before the head check and merge guard. Acceptance: cargo test passes for the whole workspace with no new warning: line in the existing CLI tests; the early PR is opened in a test with a fake host; and each new test fails without the new behavior.
